subject: Clarify: session log sampling window & deletion attestation for Clarity Health
messages:
From: security@clarityhealth.com
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@clarityhealth.com
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: extended session-level logs for investigative audit

Hi Aisha,

Quick context: Clarity is preparing for an internal clinical quality audit next quarter. Their auditors require access to session-level telemetry for a subset of user sessions for a rolling 180-day window (current Redwood default is 90 days for ephemeral session logs). We wanted to understand if Redwood can: 1) provide a targeted 180-day retention for session telemetry for a named tenant (Clarity production tenant), and 2) provide a signed attestation/certification of deletion for sessions outside the preserved subset after the 180-day window.

We attached our retention policy and a short SIG supplement that calls out this need. Primary asks: sample export format, scope of preserved fields (PII redaction), and the attestation workflow. Can you confirm feasibility and required controls?

Thanks,
Alex Munroe
Lead Security Analyst
Clarity Health

Attachment: clarity-data-retention-policy.xlsx; clarity-sig-supplement.pdf
From: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
To: security@clarityhealth.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: extended session-level logs for investigative audit

Alex — thanks for the clear note and the sample docs. I’ve looped in Ben (security / infra), Marissa (Customer Success), and Rishi (Legal) to scope a practical path. High level: we support tenant-scoped retention overrides in Redwood Private and Dedicated — we need to validate exactly which session fields you expect preserved and whether you need raw traces or a sanitized export.

Next steps I propose:
- Ben: confirm technical feasibility (storage, indexing, cost impact).
- Marissa: outline evidence deliverables and export cadence (ad-hoc vs. scheduled).
- Rishi: advise on language for attestation and any legal sign-off we need.

We can aim to provide a sample export and a draft attestation by EOD Monday (11/9). Does that timeline work?

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-sample-export-20261107.csv
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai, security@clarityhealth.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 13:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: extended session-level logs for investigative audit

Alex / team — short technical note from infra:

We can implement a tenant-specific retention profile that retains session-level telemetry for 180 days for a named tenant. Implementation notes and constraints:
- Storage: 2.3x typical cost for the preserved tenant depending on session volume; we’ll provide an estimate after we review your sample traffic patterns.
- Scope: We can preserve session metadata (timestamps, request/response hashes, model and prompt hashes, routing metadata) and a sanitized payload export that redacts user PII by default. If you require verbatim prompts/outputs we need an additional data-processing addendum due to potential PHI.
- Attestation: We can provide a machine-generated deletion certificate (signed log) when TTL expires and data is deleted. For legal attestation (executive-signed), we need a standard addendum and 10 business days to generate and countersign.
- Export: support CSV/Parquet; sample CSV attached.

Questions for Clarity: do auditors need verbatim content from the prompts/responses, or are metadata and hashes sufficient for traceability?

Ben Carter
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: security@clarityhealth.com, aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: extended session-level logs for investigative audit — evidence plan

Hi Alex — following up with the evidence plan we discussed internally. Proposed deliverables:

1) Weekly sample export (CSV, S3 redact + presigned link) for the preserved tenant containing the following columns: session_id, start_ts, end_ts, model_id, request_hash, response_hash, redacted_prompt_snippet, redaction_flags.
2) One-off bulk export on request (up to three per calendar year) containing sanitized full-text (if you add the data-processing addendum).
3) A machine-signed deletion certificate generated at TTL expiry for every session object that documents deletion timestamp and storage checksum.
4) A runbook describing our deletion pipeline, retention lifecycle, and access controls (will be shared in Drive).

Timeline: we can enable a tenant retention profile in Dedicated environments in 3 business days after contract amendment; for Hosted we require an additional security review and a 10-business-day lead time. Cost estimate and exact export format attached.

If that aligns, I’ll draft a mutual action plan and a sample schedule (kickoff, enablement, monthly evidence).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-retention-cost-estimate-clarity.pdf
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai, security@clarityhealth.com, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: extended session-level logs for investigative audit — legal framing

Alex / team — legal note on attestation and data-processing:

We can provide two levels of attestation: (A) machine-generated deletion certificates (no change to legal terms), and (B) executive-signed deletion attestation (requires a limited addendum to the MSA specifying scope, frequency, and liability cap).

For any request that includes verbatim prompts/outputs which could contain PHI/PII, we must have a data-processing addendum and confirm lawful basis for Clarity to transfer such content to their auditors. Please flag whether the auditors require raw content.

If Clarity accepts the machine-signed certificates for their audit, we can keep timelines short and proceed without contract amendments. Otherwise, allow 15–20 business days for addendum negotiation and signature.

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Legal | Redwood Inference
From: security@clarityhealth.com
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@clarityhealth.com
Date: Mon, 8 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: extended session-level logs for investigative audit — confirmation and next steps

Thanks everyone — that plan is clear and workable. For the audit the team only needs non-verbatim evidence: metadata, hashes, and redacted prompt snippets are sufficient. Clarity accepts machine-signed deletion certificates and prefers the quicker Hosted path if feasible.

Can Redwood provide the estimated incremental cost and an example presigned S3 link sample by EOD Tuesday (11/10)? Also requesting the Drive runbook once available.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Alex Munroe
Lead Security Analyst | Clarity Health
